Andy Beshear (b-SHEER; born November 29, 1977) is an American politician and attorney serving since 2019 as the 63rd governor of Kentucky.

Aung San (13 February 1915 - 19 July 1947) was a Burmese politician, independence activist and revolutionary.

Wage labor, capital accumulation, commodification, and an emphasis on innovation are the hallmarks of which profit-driven economic system?
Capitalism is an economic system based on the private ownership of the means of production and its use for the purpose of obtaining profit.

Circe (Ancient) is a witch, sometimes considered a goddess or a nymph.

Egalitarianism (from French gal 'equal'; also equalitarianism) is a school of thought within political philosophy that builds on the concept of social equality, prioritizing it for all people.

Though this exact phrase never appears in Abrahamic scripture, it describes beings cast out of Heaven for sins like pride or lust, often blamed for corrupting humanity with forbidden knowledge — what are they called?
Fallen angel are angels who were expelled from Heaven.

Garry Kasparov (born Garik Kimovich Weinstein on 13 April 1963) is a Russian chess grandmaster, political activist and writer, who was the World Chess Champion from 1985 to 2000.
Catherine the Great's lover, favorite, and possibly her consort, this Russian statesman died during the negotiations that ended his war with the Ottomans — who was he?
Grigory Potemkin was Russian military leader and statesman (1739–1791).
House speaker, secretary of state, and a three-time loser of the presidency, this Kentuckian earned the nickname 'the Great Compromiser' for defusing sectional crises — who was he?
Henry Clay (April 12, 1777 - June 29, 1852) was an American lawyer, statesman, and diplomat who represented Kentucky in both the United States House of Representatives and the United States Senate.

Humza Yousaf (born 7 April 1985) is a Scottish politician who served as First Minister of Scotland and Leader of the Scottish National Party (SNP) from March 2023 to May 2024.

Jacob is the third Hebrew patriarch in Judaism and an important figure in the Abrahamic religions.

This member of the First Triumvirate led the Gallic Wars, defeated Pompey, and sparked the political chaos that would end the Republic. Who?

Though named for one region, this Hohenzollern realm was actually based in the Margraviate of Brandenburg and rose from the work of 'The Great Elector.' What was it?
Kingdom of Prussia was a German state that existed from 1701 to 1918.
Born in Karnal to a wealthy Rajput family, this lawyer became the first prime minister of his newly founded nation and, revered as 'Leader of the Nation,' was assassinated in 1951 — who was he?
Liaquat Ali Khan (1 October 1895 - 16 October 1951) was a Pakistani lawyer, politician and statesman who served as the first prime minister of Pakistan from 1947 until his assassination in 1951.
The first Filipino to head a government of the entire Philippines, this president defeated Emilio Aguinaldo in 1935 and has a Metro Manila city named after him — who was he?

Manuel L. Quezon (19 August 1878 - 1 August 1944), also known by his initials MLQ, was a Filipino lawyer, statesman, soldier, and politician who served as the second president of the Philippines from 1935 until his death in 1944.

This Turkish politician and economist has served as Minister of Treasury and Finance since 2023, having previously been both deputy prime minister and finance minister under two different Turkish prime ministers — who is he?
Mehmet Şimşek (born 1 January 1967) is a Turkish politician and economist, who has been serving as the Minister of Treasury and Finance since 4 June 2023.
Before leading Iraq's government from 2022, this politician held an unusually long list of 'acting minister' titles, including trade, finance, and migration. Who is he?
Mohammed Shia' al-Sudani (born 4 March 1970) is an Iraqi politician and former agricultural engineer who served as the prime minister of Iraq from 2022 to 2026.

Formed in the wake of Greece's military junta collapsing in 1974, this liberal-conservative party has been one of the country's two dominant political forces for decades, long rivaling the Panhellenic Socialist Movement — what is it?

New Democracy (Greece) is a liberal-conservative political party in Greece. New Democracy and PASOK were created in the wake of the toppling of the military junta in 1974, ruling Greece in succession for the next four decades.
Born Kathleen Ruska and once known as Kath Walker, she became the first Aboriginal Australian to publish a book of verse while campaigning for Aboriginal rights. Who was she?

Oodgeroo Noonuccal (born Kathleen Jean Mary Ruska; 3 November 1920 - 16 September 1993), earlier known as Kath Walker, was an Aboriginal Australian political activist, artist and educator, who campaigned for Aboriginal rights.
This Confucian scholar-turned-revolutionary led rebel armies against French colonial forces in 19th-century Vietnam, refusing to surrender even after they desecrated his ancestral tombs. Who was he?
Phan Đình Phùng (1847 - January 21, 1896) was a Vietnamese revolutionary who led rebel armies against French colonial forces in Vietnam.
A businessman who became Lebanon's wealthiest politician, he helped forge the Taif Agreement ending the civil war and led the rebuilding of Beirut before his 2005 assassination — who was he?
Rafic Hariri (1 November 1944 - 14 February 2005) was a Lebanese businessman and politician who served as prime minister of Lebanon from 1992 to 1998 and again from 2000 to 2004.
The first Philippine president from Mindanao and the oldest to take office at 71, he had earlier served three non-consecutive terms as mayor of Davao City. Who is he?
Rodrigo Duterte (born March 28, 1945) is a Filipino politician who served as the 16th president of the Philippines from 2016 to 2022.
Originally known by a different name before it was changed, this biblical matriarch was the wife of Abraham and mother of Isaac, revered across Judaism, Christianity, and Islam — who is she?
Sarah (originally Sarai) is a biblical matriarch, prophet, and major figure in Abrahamic religions.

United Arab Republic was a country and sovereign state in the Middle East from 1958 to 1971.

War in Afghanistan (2001–2021) was a prolonged armed conflict lasting from 2001 to 2021.

Abdul Hamid II: Sultan of the Ottoman Empire from 1876 to 1909.

Aztecs: Ethnic group of central Mexico and its civilization.

Ding Xuexiang: First-ranking Vice Premier of China since 2023.

Edmund Ironside: King of England in 1016. Edmund's reign was spent fighting against a Danish invasion led by Cnut.

End of World War II in Europe

False Dmitry I: Tsar of Russia from 1605 to 1606.
A longtime aide to Gerhard Schröder before serving as Germany's top diplomat twice, he has been President of Germany since 2017 — who is he?

Frank-Walter Steinmeier: President of Germany since 2017. Frank-Walter Steinmeier (German: [ˈfʁaŋkˌvaltɐ ˈʃtaɪnˌmaɪ.ɐ]; born 5 January 1956) is a German politician who has served as President of Germany since 2017.
Born in Rostock and later a Prussian field marshal, this military leader helped defeat Napoleon at the Battle of Leipzig in 1813 and again at Waterloo in 1815 — who is he?
Gebhard Leberecht von Blücher: Prussian field marshal (1742–1819)
According to Exodus, the Israelites made this idol of a young bovine while Moses was away on Mount Sinai — what was it?
Golden calf: Idol in the Torah, the Bible, and the Quran.
He became the fifteenth ruler of an Arabian dynasty in 2020 after his cousin's death, having previously served for decades as Minister of Heritage and Culture — who is he?
Haitham bin Tariq: Sultan of Oman since 2020.

Said to be the most beautiful woman in the world and a daughter of Zeus, her elopement with a foreign prince triggered a legendary decade-long war after her first husband, the Spartan king, lost her — who was she?
Helen of Troy: Most beautiful woman in Greek mythology.
Owned by Cover Corporation, this virtual YouTuber talent agency manages dozens of streamers across three languages with a combined 80 million-plus subscribers — what is it?
Hololive Production: Japanese virtual YouTuber agency. In December 2019, Hololive was merged with Cover's male Holostars agency and INoNaKa music label under the unified "Hololive Production" brand.
A young military officer with a geology degree from Ouagadougou, he seized power as interim president of Burkina Faso after a 2022 coup, championing pan-Africanist and anti-Western views. Who is he?
Ibrahim Traoré: Leader of Burkina Faso since 2022.

Formed in 1946 by former supporters of Benito Mussolini's Republican Fascist Party, which political party became postwar Italy's fourth-largest by the early 1960s while presenting itself as the defender of fascism's legacy?
Italian Social Movement: Neo-fascist political party, 1946–1955.

Janata Dal (United): Political party in India.

Born under a cloud of doubt about his parentage after his mother's captivity by a rival tribe, this early Mongol Empire prince became a military commander and the ancestor of the rulers of the Golden Horde — who is he?
Jochi: Mongol prince and general (c. 1182 – c. 1225)
Publishing a new scripture at age 24, this American founder of a major religious movement drew tens of thousands of followers before his death just fourteen years later — who was he?
Joseph Smith: Founder of the Latter Day Saint movement (1805–1844)

Karel Schwarzenberg: Czech politician and noble (1937–2023)

Kingdom of Bohemia: Monarchy in Central Europe (1198–1918)
This Guinean general seized power in a 1984 coup and then ruled the West African nation as its second president until his death in 2008 — who was he?
Lansana Conté: President of Guinea from 1984 to 2008.

Marcos Pérez Jiménez: Dictator of Venezuela from 1952 to 1958. The economy of Venezuela developed rapidly while Pérez was in power.
This US Army general led the 82nd Airborne in Sicily, Italy and Normandy, later commanded a corps at the Battle of the Bulge, and went on to be Supreme Allied Commander Europe — who was he?
Matthew Ridgway: United States Army general (1895–1993)
A Catholic priest revered as the Father of the Nation, he delivered the famous 'Cry of Dolores' on 16 September 1810 to launch Mexico's independence movement — who is he?
Miguel Hidalgo y Costilla: Mexican Catholic preacher (1753–1811)
Born in Mashhad and the second son of Iran's second supreme leader, this cleric commanded the Basij militia from 2009 and became his country's third supreme leader in 2026 — who is he?

Mojtaba Khamenei: Supreme Leader of Iran since 2026. Mojtaba Hosseini Khamenei (born 8 September 1969) is an Iranian cleric and politician who has served as the third supreme leader of Iran since 2026.

Crowned King of Rome at birth and later nicknamed 'the Eaglet,' he was the disputed Emperor of the French for all of two weeks in 1815 before living out his days in Vienna — which son of a famous conqueror?
Napoleon II: Disputed Emperor of the French in 1815 (1811–1832)
Shared across Jainism, Hinduism, Buddhism, and Sikhism, this state of liberation marks the end of the cycle of rebirth and the extinguishing of worldly passions — what is it?
Nirvana: Liberation from repeated rebirth in saṃsāra.
Having joined the Italian resistance as a teenager in World War II, this journalist grew famous for fierce interviews with the likes of Henry Kissinger, Golda Meir, and the Shah of Iran — who is she?
Oriana Fallaci: Italian journalist and author (1929–2006)

This semi-nomadic Turkic people controlled the steppes of southeastern Europe and Crimea in the 9th and 10th centuries, waging war against the early Rus' state for over two hundred years — who were they?
Pechenegs: Extinct Turkic people. The Pechenegs or Patzinaks, were a semi-nomadic Turkic people from Central Asia who spoke the Pecheneg language.
Serving as the 64th Bishop of Rome from 590 until 604, this former Roman prefect sent missionaries to England, including Augustine of Canterbury — who was he?
Pope Gregory I: 64th Bishop of Rome; head of the Roman Catholic Church from AD 590 to 604.

Founded in 1891 by Leandro N. Alem, this Argentine political party is the country's second-oldest active party and a longtime human-rights advocate that has been banned under military rule — which party?
Radical Civic Union: Political party in Argentina. The Radical Civic Union (Spanish: Unión Cívica Radical, UCR) is a major political party in Argentina.
Known by the abbreviation PRO and led by former Argentine president Mauricio Macri, which party has governed Buenos Aires since 2007?
Republican Proposal: Political party in Argentina.
Born in Hong Kong and educated at Eton, this British former diplomat and MP walked solo across Asia after leaving the Foreign Office, and now co-hosts a podcast with Alastair Campbell — who is he?

Stefano Bandecchi: Italian politician and entrepreneur. Stefano Bandecchi (born 4 April 1961) is an Italian politician and entrepreneur.
Reigning over the Georgian Golden Age from 1184 to 1213, this Bagrationi monarch was the first woman to rule Georgia in her own right and was given the title 'King' in medieval sources — who was she?
Tamar I: Queen of Georgia from 1184 to 1213. Tamar was successful in neutralizing this opposition and embarked on an energetic foreign policy aided by the decline of the hostile Seljuk Turks.

This South Australian premier governed for over 26 years — the longest unbroken stretch of any elected leader in Australian history — and was famous for shamelessly haranguing federal leaders into funding his state. Who was he?
Thomas Playford IV: 20th-century Australian politician and fruit grower (1896–1981)
This Indian politician served as Maharashtra's 19th chief minister from 2019 to 2022 while also editing a newspaper for over a decade — who is he?
Uddhav Thackeray: 19th Chief Minister of Maharashtra from 2019 to 2022 (born 1960)
In 1976, this Soviet pilot defected to the West by flying his MiG-25 'Foxbat' jet interceptor to Japan, handing the CIA what George H. W. Bush called an 'intelligence bonanza' — who is he?

Beginning with the 1916 death of Yuan Shikai, this chaotic decade-plus in Chinese history saw the country splinter under rival military cliques until Sun Yat-sen's Nationalists challenged the Beijing government for legitimacy — which period?
Warlord Era: Period in the history of the Republic of China (1916–1928)
First achieved in Australasia before spreading to Europe and the Americas, this democratic right for female voters began its 'first wave' in 1893 in English-speaking countries — what right?
Women's suffrage: Legal right of women to vote.
A close associate of Gandhi and a founder of Jamia Millia Islamia, this Berlin-educated educationist rose to become president of India, dying in office in 1969 — who was he?
Zakir Husain: President of India from 1967 to 1969.
Who among these was born first?
Georges Dumézil (born 1898) is the earliest of the four.
Who among these was born first?
William Osler (born 1849) is the earliest of the four.
Which of these four dates back furthest?
Lisp (programming language) (founded 1958) is the earliest of the four.
Which of these came out first?
TeX (published 1978) is the earliest of the four.
Which one below is best known as a physicist?
Vikram Sarabhai is a physicist. Often regarded as the "Father of Indian space program", Sarabhai was honored with Padma Bhushan in 1966 and the Padma Vibhushan (posthumously) in 1972.
Who among these is a chemist?
Glenn T. Seaborg is a chemist. Throughout his career, Seaborg worked for arms control.
What is the atomic number of Beryllium?
Beryllium is a chemical element; it has symbol Be and atomic number 4.
In what year was Galileo Galilei born?
Galileo Galilei: Galileo has been called the father of observational astronomy, modern-era classical physics, the scientific method, and modern science.
In what year was Caesium discovered?
Caesium (IUPAC spelling; also spelled cesium in American English) is a chemical element; it has symbol Cs and atomic number 55.
In what year was Osmium discovered?
Osmium (from Ancient Greek ὀσμή (osmḗ) 'smell') is a chemical element; it has symbol Os and atomic number 76.
Which company manufactures AIDC F-CK-1 Ching-kuo?
AIDC F-CK-1 Ching-kuo: Aerospace Industrial Development Corporation. The aircraft made its first flight in 1989.
In which country is Virgo interferometer?
Virgo interferometer: Italy. The Virgo interferometer is a large-scale scientific instrument near Pisa, Italy, for detecting gravitational waves.
Who is credited with discovering Gaussian integral?
Gaussian integral: Leonhard Euler. The integral has a wide range of applications.
Who is credited with discovering Aspirin?
Aspirin: Raffaele Piria. Aspirin is used to treat inflammatory conditions including Kawasaki disease, pericarditis, and rheumatic fever.
Who is credited with discovering Boron?
Boron: Joseph Louis Gay-Lussac. Boron is a chemical element; it has symbol B and atomic number 5.

The active component of vinegar and the second simplest carboxylic acid, this colourless liquid with the formula CH₃COOH has been produced in large quantities since the third millennium BCE. What is this acid?
Acetic acid is an acidic, colourless liquid and organic compound with the chemical formula CH3COOH (also written as CH3CO2H, C2H4O2, or HC2H3O2).
A close relative of the peach in the genus Prunus, this drupe's seed isn't a true nut and can be "blanched" by softening its skin in hot water before peeling — what is it?
Nicknamed 'the heart of the scorpion,' this distinctly reddish variable star is the brightest in the constellation Scorpius — what is it?
Antares is the brightest star in the constellation of Scorpius. It has the Bayer designation α Scorpii, which is Latinised to Alpha Scorpii.
With atomic number 85 and symbol At, this is the rarest naturally occurring element in Earth's crust, forming only as a decay product of heavier elements — name it?
Astatine is a chemical element; it has symbol At and atomic number 85.
Designed to replace the aging Tu-126 'Moss,' this Soviet early-warning aircraft saw only about 42 built before the USSR's breakup ended production in 1992 — what is it?
Beriev A-50 (NATO reporting name: Mainstay) is a Soviet-origin airborne early warning and control (AEW&C) aircraft that is based on the Ilyushin Il-76 transport plane.
Accepted by the American Kennel Club in 1893, this small, compact dog breed with a short tail and erect ears originated in the United States — name the breed?
Boston Terrier is a breed of dog originating in the United States of America.
Its common name is a contraction of 'Mary's gold,' honoring the Virgin Mary, but this daisy-family genus's Latin name nods to the calendar instead — which flowering plant?
Calendula is a genus of about 15-20 species of annual and perennial herbaceous plants in the daisy family, Asteraceae that are often known as marigolds.
Their name is Greek for "head-feet," and fishers sometimes call them "inkfish" for their ink-squirting trick; squid, octopus and nautilus all belong. What's this molluscan class?
Cephalopod is any member of the molluscan class Cephalopoda (Greek plural, kephalpodes; "head-feet") such as a squid, octopus, cuttlefish, or nautilus.
This common name covers many species of bivalve mollusc that use a powerful foot to burrow into sand or mud, with two equal shells joined by adductor muscles — what creature is it?
Clam is a common name for several species of bivalve mollusc. In culinary usage, clams are commonly eaten marine bivalves, as in clam digging and the resulting soup, clam chowder.
A genus of over 260 fungi, most of them parasites that bore into insects and other arthropods, this 'club-headed' organism has 1,500 years of use in Chinese medicine — what is it?
Cordyceps is a genus of ascomycete fungi (sac fungi) that includes over 260 species worldwide, many of which are parasitic.
Born at the Point McLeay Mission in 1872, this preacher and inventor who registered 10 patents is widely credited as the first Aboriginal Australian published author — who is he?
David Unaipon was an Aboriginal Australian preacher, inventor, and writer who has been widely credited as the first Aboriginal published author.
This scarab superfamily insect is famous for rolling balls of animal droppings, a behavior the Ancient Egyptians linked to the god Khepri — which creature is it?
Dung beetle are beetles that feed on feces.
This inflammation of the small intestine is most often caused by contaminated food or drink, though NSAIDs, radiation, and autoimmune conditions can also trigger it. What is it?
Enteritis is inflammation of the small intestine. Duodenitis, jejunitis, and ileitis are subtypes of enteritis which are localised to a specific part of the small intestine.
This mutual prodrug fuses amphetamine and theophylline into one molecule, marketed as a psychostimulant and better known today as a smuggled illicit street drug — what compound is it?
Fenethylline (BAN, USAN) or fenetylline (INN) is a codrug of amphetamine and theophylline and so a mutual prodrug of both.
This American video game businessman dropped out of Harvard to join Microsoft, where he worked on early Windows and a Doom port, before co-founding Valve Corporation in 1996 — who is he?
Gabe Newell (born November 3, 1962), also known by his nickname GabeN, is an American video game developer and businessman.

This small freshwater fish, native to China and one of the world's most popular aquarium pets, has become an invasive pest after being released into wild waterways in North America and Australia — what fish is it?
Goldfish (Carassius auratus) is a freshwater fish in the family Cyprinidae of the order Cypriniformes.

This now-outdated astronomical model placed the Sun rather than the Earth at the center of the universe, eventually replacing the geocentric view before itself being superseded by relativity — what model is it?
Heliocentrism (also known as the heliocentric model) is a superseded astronomical model that placed the Sun at the center of the universe, with the Earth and the planets in its orbit.

Also called prussic acid, this highly toxic and flammable liquid boils just above room temperature at 25.6 degrees Celsius. It is produced industrially as a precursor to many chemical compounds, particularly potassium cyanide and adiponitrile. What is it?
Hydrogen cyanide (also called prussic acid) is a chemical compound with the formula HCN and structural formula HCN.
Founder of Romania's Social Democratic Party, this engineer served two separate stints as president after playing a leading role in the 1989 revolution that toppled Ceaușescu — who is he?

Ion Iliescu (3 March 1930 - 5 August 2025) was a Romanian politician and engineer who served as the first and third President of Romania since the country's transition to democracy, from 1990 to 1996 and 2000 to 2004.
England's very first Astronomer Royal, he compiled a 3,000-star catalogue and even spotted Uranus — though he mistakenly logged it as a star. Who was he?
John Flamsteed (19 August 1646 - 31 December 1719) was an English astronomer and the first Astronomer Royal.
Named after a 19th-century Russian neuropsychiatrist, which memory disorder features confabulation and amnesia from vitamin B1 deficiency, often following an episode of Wernicke encephalopathy?
Korsakoff syndrome (KS) is a disorder of the central nervous system characterized by amnesia, deficits in explicit memory, and confabulation.

This scientific discipline studies language through areas like syntax, semantics, morphology, and phonology, with subfields examining its biological roots and psychological underpinnings — name the field?
Linguistics is the scientific study of language. Linguistics encompasses many branches and subfields that span both theoretical and practical applications.

With degrees from Stanford in chemical engineering and a medical degree from Cornell, this physician-astronaut spent nearly eight days aboard Endeavour in 1992, becoming the first African-American woman in space — who is she?
Mae Jemison (born October 17, 1956) is an American engineer, physician, and former NASA astronaut.
Most common on the legs in women and the back in men, this cancer develops from melanin-producing skin cells and, in extremely rare cases, can even arise in the lungs — which cancer?
Melanoma is a type of cancer, typically skin cancer; it develops from the melanin-producing cells known as melanocytes.
This small, subterranean mammal has velvety fur, tiny eyes, and short powerful forelimbs with oversized paws built for constant digging — what animal is it?

It's the inherent character of the universe as a whole — the laws, elements, and phenomena of the physical world, including life itself — even though humans are often spoken of as somehow apart from it. What is it?
Nature is an inherent character or constitution, particularly of the ecosphere or the universe as a whole.
This massive bony fish, weighing up to a metric ton, resembles a giant fish head without a tail and is native to tropical and temperate waters worldwide. What is it?
Ocean sunfish (Mola mola), also known as the common mola, is one of the largest bony fish in the world.

Nicknamed the 'white rats' of its phylum for how often it's used in classroom and lab experiments, this single-celled ciliate thrives in freshwater, brackish, and marine habitats — what organism is it?
Paramecium ((ee-)m, -see-m, plural "paramecia" only when used as a vernacular name) is a genus of eukaryotic, unicellular ciliates, widespread in freshwater, brackish, and marine environments.
This herbaceous annual vine produces edible pods and comes in bush or climbing cultivars; global output hit 28 million tonnes in 2022, led by India. What legume species is it?
Phaseolus vulgaris is a herbaceous annual plant. Its botanical classification, along with other Phaseolus species, is as a member of the legume family, Fabaceae.

This medical condition occurs when air collects in the space between the lung and chest wall, typically causing sudden, sharp one-sided chest pain and shortness of breath — what's the condition called?
Pneumothorax is collection of air in the pleural space between the lung and the chest wall.
This thorny European shrub's tart fruit flavors a British gin, while its tough wood traditionally makes an Irish walking stick — what plant is it (scientific name)?
Prunus spinosa is a species of flowering plant in the rose family, Rosaceae.
First flown in 1955 as a nuclear-strike follow-on to the Mach 1 Super Sabre, this fighter-bomber earned the nickname 'Thud' and flew most early Vietnam War strike missions — which aircraft?
Republic F-105 Thunderchief is an American fighter-bomber that served with the United States Air Force from 1958 to 1984.
One of the world's oldest crops, this thistle-like annual plant with globular orange or red flower heads is grown commercially today for oil pressed from its seeds — what is it?
Safflower (Carthamus tinctorius), also false saffron, is a highly branched, herbaceous, thistle-like annual plant in the family Asteraceae.
About 90% of the body's supply of this mood-regulating monoamine is actually made in the gut, where it helps drive intestinal movements — which neurotransmitter is it?
Serotonin (5-HT), is a monoamine neurotransmitter with a wide range of functions in both the central nervous system (CNS) and also peripheral tissues.
Known in Hispanic America as guanábana and easily killed by a touch of frost, which Annona fruit blends flavors of strawberry, apple, and sour citrus?
Soursop (also called graviola, guyabano, and in Hispanic America guanbana) is the fruit of Annona muricata, a broadleaf, flowering, evergreen tree.
The only surviving tiger population in the Sunda Islands, found on the Indonesian island of Sumatra after its Bali and Javan cousins went extinct in the 20th century — what is it?
Sumatran tiger is a population of Panthera tigris sondaica on the Indonesian island of Sumatra.
What academic discipline studies religious belief from within a faith perspective, focusing on the nature of divinity, revelation, and the history behind organized religion?
Theology is the study of religious belief from a religious perspective, with a focus on the nature of divinity and the history behind religion.
Named for the compulsive pulling of one's own hair, this disorder brings a brief positive feeling with each pull but is notoriously hard to stop — what is it?
Trichotillomania (TTM), also known as hair-pulling disorder or compulsive hair pulling, is a mental disorder characterized by a long-term urge that results in the pulling out of one's own hair.
Known also as sight or eyesight, this sense lets the body detect photons and build a picture of its environment using daytime or night modes — what is it?
Visual perception is the ability to detect light and use it to form an image of the surrounding environment.

An Iranian-born American surgeon specializing in bariatric and vascular procedures, this reality TV doctor became known for helping morbidly obese patients lose weight on the long-running series My 600-lb Life — name this doctor?
Younan Nowzaradan (born October 11, 1944), also known as Dr.
A pseudoscientific but ancient component of traditional Chinese medicine, this practice involves inserting thin needles into the body, most often for pain relief — what is it called?
Coined in 1852 but now considered stigmatizing in clinical settings, this WHO-estimated 283-million-person global condition involves continued drinking despite the harm it causes — what is it called?
Over 500 of these organic compounds exist in nature, yet only 22 appear in the genetic code, joining together to build proteins — what are they?
Amino acid: Organic compounds containing amine and carboxylic groups.

Serving as Surveyor of the Queen's Pictures while secretly working as the 'fourth man' of a notorious spy ring, this British art historian wrote a landmark 1967 study of the painter Nicolas Poussin — who is he?
Anthony Blunt: British art historian and Soviet spy (1907–1983)
Painting, sculpture, and architecture are its three classical visual branches, yet nobody can agree on a single definition for it; what cultural pursuit of creative and imaginative talent is this?
Art: Creative work to evoke aesthetic response.
The world's largest nocturnal primate, this Madagascar lemur has ever-growing rodent-like teeth and taps tree trunks with a bony middle finger to fish out grubs by echo — which animal?
Aye-aye: Species of primate. This foraging method is called percussive foraging, and takes up 5–41% of the aye-aye's foraging time.
Sold under the brand name Tessalon, this cough-relief medication works within about 20 minutes by acting as a local anesthetic that blocks stretch receptors in the lungs — what is this drug called?
Benzonatate: Oral cough medication. Benzonatate, sold under the brand name Tessalon among others, is a medication that is used for the symptomatic relief of cough.

Native to North America and classified in the genus Vaccinium, this fruit comes in wild 'lowbush' and cultivated 'highbush' varieties, with Canada leading global production of the wild type — what fruit is it?
Blueberry: Perennial plant with blue berries.
This rhythmic process of inhaling and exhaling delivers oxygen to the alveoli and removes carbon dioxide, with its per-minute rate counted as a vital sign — what is it?
Breathing: Process of moving air in and out of the lungs.
Found in chalk, limestone, eggshells, and pearls alike, this CaCO3 compound is also the active ingredient in agricultural lime and doubles as an antacid — what is it?
Calcium carbonate: Chemical compound. Materials containing much calcium carbonate or resembling it are described as calcareous.

Discovered as a single well-preserved skeleton in Argentina's Chubut Province in 1984, this short-snouted, lightly built predator belongs to a South American branch of large theropods — which dinosaur genus?
Carnotaurus: Genus of dinosaur from the Late Cretaceous period.
With independently swiveling eyes, a projectile tongue, and the ability to shift colors, this Old World lizard family is famous for camouflage — which reptile?
Chameleon: Family of reptiles. The members of this family are best known for their distinct range of colours, being capable of colour-shifting camouflage.
Named from Latin words meaning 'around' and 'day,' this roughly 24-hour internal biological cycle appears independently across animals, plants, fungi, and cyanobacteria?
Circadian rhythm: Natural internal process that regulates the sleep-wake cycle.
This bird family contains both doves and pigeons — including the feral rock dove common in cities — spanning 52 genera and 353 species worldwide. What's the family called?
Columbidae: Family of birds. The bird most commonly referred to as "pigeon" is the domestic pigeon, descendant of the wild rock dove, which is a common inhabitant of cities as the feral pigeon.
First described in 1880 by a French neurologist, this rare delusion convinces sufferers that they are dead, don't exist, or have lost their internal organs — what is it called?
Cotard's syndrome: Delusion that one is dead or non-existent.
Bred in Germany with short legs and a long body to chase badgers into their burrows, which hound breed comes in smooth-, wire-, and long-haired varieties?
Sold as Voltaren and taken by mouth, suppository, injection, skin gel, or even eye drops, this NSAID eases pain and inflammation like gout for up to eight hours a dose — what is it?
Revered by Ancient Egyptians as the god Khepri for rolling the sun across the sky, which insect feeds exclusively on feces?
Dung beetle: Informal group of insects.
Born in Pretoria and once a Zip2 co-founder, this CEO of Tesla and SpaceX became, by some estimates, the first dollar trillionaire in 2026 — who is he?
Elon Musk: Businessman and public official (born 1971)
Also called moral philosophy, this field splits into normative, applied, and meta- branches as it asks what people ought to do and whether objective moral facts even exist. Which discipline is it?
Birds of prey in the genus Falco, some small species are called hobbies and hover-hunters are called kestrels — what are they collectively known as?
Falcon: Birds of prey in the genus Falco. The largest falcon is the gyrfalcon at up to 65 cm (26 in) in length.
Members of the order Siphonaptera, these flightless blood-sucking parasites can leap 50 times their own body length — what are they?
Flea: Insects of the order Siphonaptera. Flea, the common name for the order Siphonaptera, includes 2,500 species of small flightless insects that live as external parasites of mammals and birds.
This Canadian physician and author has written five books linking childhood trauma to conditions like ADHD and addiction, though critics question the evidence behind some claims — who is he?
Caused by a genetic variant in the UGT1A1 gene, this harmless liver condition slows the breakdown of bilirubin and can trigger jaundice during stress, exercise, or fasting — what is it called?
Gilbert's syndrome: Medical condition. It is typically inherited in an autosomal recessive pattern and occasionally in an autosomal dominant pattern depending on the type of variant.
An Augustinian friar and abbot in Brno, this Austrian biologist spent 1856 to 1863 crossbreeding pea plants — work that earned him posthumous fame as the founder of genetics. Who was he?
Gregor Mendel: Austrian biologist and friar (1822–1884)

This English physician co-wrote the first English-language medical textbook on homosexuality in 1897, coined the term 'narcissism,' and penned an early public account of a mescaline trip he took on himself. Who was he?
Havelock Ellis: British physician, eugenicist, writer, and social reformer (1859–1939)
Its name means 'river horse' in Ancient Greek, yet this semiaquatic sub-Saharan giant — the largest even-toed ungulate alive — is more closely tied to pigs than to horses; what is it?
Hippopotamus: Species of large semi-aquatic mammal.
Marketed as Buscopan, this anticholinergic medication treats abdominal cramps, bladder and biliary spasms, and can ease respiratory secretions near the end of life — what drug is it?
Hyoscine butylbromide: Anticholinergic medication. It is also used to improve excessive respiratory secretions at the end of life.
An application of computer science, this field covers not just computers and networks but also distribution technologies like television and telephones — what is it?
Information technology: Computer-based technologies. Whisler commented that "the new technology does not yet have a single established name.

While working as an instrument maker at the University of Glasgow, this Scottish engineer's separate-condenser design transformed Newcomen's steam engine into the machine that powered the Industrial Revolution — who was he?
James Watt: Scottish inventor, engineer and chemist (1736–1819)

A Columbia economist and former World Bank chief economist who won the 2001 Nobel, he champions Georgism and skewers the "free-market fundamentalists" he blames for mismanaging globalization — who is he?
Joseph Stiglitz: American economist and Nobel Laureate (born 1943)
Also called German turnip despite not being related to true turnips, this stout cabbage cultivar can be eaten raw or cooked, stem and leaves alike — what vegetable?
Kohlrabi: Biennial cultivar of wild cabbage.

This small wild feline of South and Southeast Asia sports dark spots on a tawny coat and two stripes running from its eyes to its ears, and can live as high as 4,474 meters in the Himalayas — what is it?
Leopard cat: Small wild cat species. The leopard cat (Prionailurus bengalensis) is a small wild cat with dark spots on the tawny-coloured body and limbs.

Developed under the US Air Force's Advanced Tactical Fighter program, this American twin-engine stealth fighter was designed for air superiority but also handles ground attack, electronic warfare and signals intelligence — which aircraft?

Lockheed Martin F-22 Raptor: American stealth air superiority fighter. The Lockheed Martin–Boeing F-22 Raptor is an American twin-engine, jet-powered, all-weather, supersonic stealth fighter aircraft.
Element number 12 is so eager to ignite that, once lit, it burns with a brilliant-white light — this lightweight alkaline-earth metal, less dense than aluminium, is what?
Magnesium: Chemical element with atomic number 12 (Mg)
Part of the chamomile tribe within the sunflower family, some species in this plant genus share the common name 'mayweed' — which genus?
Discovered in 1893 and existing as two mirror-image enantiomers, this CNS stimulant is best known in its hydrochloride-salt form nicknamed 'crystal' — what is it?
This synthetic prostaglandin medication treats stomach ulcers, induces labor, and — often paired with mifepristone — is used to end a pregnancy. What drug is it?
Misoprostol: Medication to induce abortion and treat ulcers.
Considered a cultural universal present in every human society, this medium arranges sound into harmony, melody, and rhythm through composition, improvisation, and performance — what is it?
Music: Form of art using sound.
Erected by entomologist Francis Walker back in 1855, this genus of moths belongs to the family Lasiocampidae — which genus?
This biochemical process lets an organism turn food and water into energy and building blocks, and can go wrong with too much or too little of certain essential substances — what process?
Nutrition: Provision to cells and organisms to support life.
In young children it can mean ear-pulling, extra crying, and poor sleep; it's a group of inflammatory diseases of the middle ear, from acute infections to lingering fluid. What's the medical name?
Otitis media: Inflammation of the middle ear. One of the two main types is acute otitis media (AOM), an infection of rapid onset that usually presents with ear pain.
Cultivated across the tropics for its fragrant essential oil, over 90% of this mint-family herb's global oil supply now comes from Indonesia — which plant?
This legume's raw seeds contain a toxic compound that must be boiled away before eating, though its unripe green pods are eaten as-is — which species is it?
Named from a Greek word meaning 'wanderers,' these large rounded bodies orbit a star or similar object — our solar system has eight, from Mercury to Neptune. What are they called?
Planet: Large, round non-stellar astronomical object.
Marked by high blood pressure and protein in the urine after 20 weeks of pregnancy, this disorder can progress to seizures if left untreated — what is it called?
Excess fluid pooling in the lungs' air sacs impairs oxygen exchange and can be triggered by either heart failure or a range of unrelated causes — what condition is this?
Pulmonary edema: Fluid accumulation in the tissue and air spaces of the lungs.
This bird of prey, related to eagles and buzzards, now breeds only in Europe but has wandered as far as Finland and the Gambia — what raptor is it?
Red kite: Species of bird. The red kite (Milvus milvus) is a bird of prey in the family Accipitridae, which also includes many other diurnal raptors such as eagles, buzzards, and harriers.
Defined by a single pair of ever-growing incisors in each jaw, this mammalian order makes up about 40 percent of all mammal species — which order?
Rodent: Order of mammals. The rodent fossil record dates back to the Paleocene of Asia.
Commonly known as elder, with its blossoms called elderflower and its fruit elderberry, this genus contains between 20 and 30 flowering plant species — which genus?
When an infection-triggered immune overreaction sends blood pressure plummeting and disrupts cells throughout the body, doctors in the ICU are treating this life-threatening condition — what is it?
Septic shock: Dangerously low blood pressure due to damage from an organ infection.
Roughly 21 feet long yet coiled to fit inside the abdomen, this digestive tube receives bile and pancreatic juice and is divided into the duodenum, jejunum, and ileum — which organ?
Small intestine: Organ in the gastrointestinal tract.
Commonly nicknamed phlegm, this mucus coughed up from the trachea and bronchi is examined for tell-tale yellow or green coloring that signals infection — what is it?
Sputum: Mucus that is coughed up from the lower airways.

Serving under both Presidents Sukarno and Suharto, this Indonesian economist held posts across trade, finance, and research ministries, and once lobbied Washington against Dutch colonial rule — who was he?
Sumitro Djojohadikusumo: Indonesian statesman and economist (1917–2001)
The earliest known example was the stone tool, and the later control of fire is even credited with helping grow the human brain and spark language — what broad field is being described?
Technology: Use of knowledge for practical goals.
Native to the Mediterranean and containing roughly 350 aromatic species, this herb genus lends its name to a common seasoning found in kitchens worldwide — which genus?
About 70% of people infected with this parasite-caused sexually transmitted infection show no symptoms at all, though it can raise the risk of contracting HIV — what condition is it?
Trichomoniasis: Medical condition. Trichomoniasis (trich) is an infectious disease caused by the parasite Trichomonas vaginalis.

Known by names like lingonberry and cowberry, this evergreen shrub's tart berries are a Nordic cuisine staple and are commercially grown in the Pacific Northwest and the Netherlands — what is its scientific name?
Vaccinium vitis-idaea: Species of shrub with edible fruit.
Tasteless, odorless, and nearly colorless, this polar molecule's strong hydrogen bonding makes it the solvent inside every known living organism — yet it offers no food energy at all. What is it?
Water: Chemical compound of hydrogen and oxygen.
Based on how long Earth takes to orbit the Sun, this unit of time comes in tropical and sidereal forms differing by about 20 minutes, with leap years keeping our calendar in sync — what unit?

Year: Unit of time based on Earth's orbit. In scientific use, the tropical year (approximately 365 solar days, 5 hours, 48 minutes, 45 seconds) and the sidereal year (about 20 minutes longer) are more exact.

What is the chemical symbol for nickel?
The symbol for nickel is Ni. Nickel is a chemical element; it has symbol Ni and atomic number 28.
